ImageDescription.value: The main facade of Smøla Town Hall, completed with municipal offices in 1989, located on Rådhusveien in the village of Hopen, situated in the northern part of the island of Smøla in Møre og Romsdal County, Norway. ObjectName.value: VEIHOLMEN fiskevær fishing village Smøla 2024-09-11 Skilt peker til hovedsteder for 33 nasjonaliteter Smøla jan. 2023 (Fingerpost 33 nationalities) IMG 9354

Categories.value: Smøla|Immigrants to Norway|Directional signposts|Veiholmen|Self-published work|Fingerposts in Norway|Norway photographs taken on 2024-09-11

ImageDescription.value:
Photo from Veiholmen, a former fishing village located on a group of tiny islands in the northern part of Smøla Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway, taken on a September morning in 2024.

The image shows the buildings and landscape in the weather-exposed archipelago, with islands and islets, a lighthouse (coastal lantern) at the entrance from the island of Hottranklakken to Skjærgårdsveien road, and a lamppost with signs or direction indicators pointing towards and showing the distance to the capitals of the countries from which the 33 nationalities that lived on Smøla in January 2023 originated.

Veiholmen is located at the end of a 7-kilometre (4.3 mi) long road leading north from the village of Hopen. The road goes over many islands connecting Veiholmen to the island of Smøla to the south. In 2015, the village had the population of 212. For some time, Veiholmen was one of Norway's largest fishing villages located south of Lofoten, but it has declined significantly throughout the 20th century. Today, Veiholmen is a popular place for tourists in the spring, summer, and autumn, with tourist attractions and very good fishing opportunities.
